ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a 2×4 table. The first row from left to right is 10, 13, 20, 26, and the second row from left to right is 3, 7, 6, 14, so the four columns are respectively (10,3), (13,7), (20,6), (26,14). Reasoning: From adjacent columns in the figure, the rule can be confirmed: if the previous column is (a,b), then the upper entry of the next column is a+b, and the lower entry is a-b. For example, (10,3) becomes (13,7), because 10+3=13 and 10-3=7. Carl's table is 2×7, so from the first column to the last column there are 6 changes in total. The last column is (96,64). Use the rule in reverse: if the next column is (s,d), then the previous column is ((s+d)/2,(s-d)/2). Work backward 6 times in sequence: (96,64) -> ((96+64)/2,(96-64)/2) = (80,16) (80,16) -> (48,32) (48,32) -> (40,8) (40,8) -> (24,16) (24,16) -> (20,4) (20,4) -> (12,8) So the first column is (12,8), and its sum is 12+8=20.
